$comment: Benchmark decks from sub-phase 0.8. The decks themselves are NOT committed - the largest is 188 MiB - so what is here is the recipe, the exact size and the SHA-256 of the file that recipe produces. The generator is deterministic, so anyone can rebuild a deck and check they have the same one. Every entry carries a `license`, which sub-phase 1.1 makes a CI-enforced requirement for the whole corpus.

entries.source: synthetic feature probe generated by our own tooling
entries.description: The plan's own envelope for sub-phase 0.8: 300 slides at about 200 MB, dominated by media, which is the shape a real large deck has. Every image is incompressible noise, because a deck padded with zeroes deflates away and the ZIP reader then never does the work a real file makes it do. Opens in PowerPoint 365 with no repair prompt: 300 slides, 6 sections, and 5191 shapes - the same number the generator allocated ids for.

entries.path: (not committed - 4.4 MiB on disk, 87 MiB inflated)
entries.source: synthetic feature probe generated by our own tooling
entries.description: The same 300 slides with no media and 400 shapes each. The media deck cannot exercise the tokenizer at all - 184 of its 188 MiB never reach the XML layer - and this one is the case whose throughput actually predicts anything about phase 2 onwards. It also probes the decompression budget: 4.4 MiB in, 87 MiB out, a 20:1 ratio across the archive.

entries.source: synthetic feature probe generated by our own tooling
entries.description: Twenty slides with every feature at least twice, for opening in PowerPoint by hand and for the test suite. tools/bench/bench.test.ts builds this recipe and checks the census finds exactly the features the generator put in - two independently written counts of the same file. Opens in PowerPoint 365 with no repair prompt.

embeddedFont.$comment: Every recipe embeds the CC0 probe font sub-phase 0.7 authored, and a run on the first slide uses it. Nothing anyone else owns is embedded in a file this project hands around.
